newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna's ATX extends gains, seen heading for 1,200.
newsitem.headline: Vienna's ATX extends gains, seen heading for 1,200.

text.p: Austria's blue-chip ATX index ended with solid gains on Thursday with traders forecasting a push for 1,200 points after tomorrow's expiry of futures contracts is out of the way.
Traders said sentiment was buoyed by a dwindling presence of active sellers.
"Bullish," one trader summed up sentiment. "The aggressive sellers seem to be done."
The ATX index gained 0.73 percent, or 8.53 points, to 1,179.48 after a tentative start. Of its 21 constituents, 12 advanced, eight fell and one was unchanged by the close.
Traders cited genuine investor demand behind today's buying, especially in steelmaker VA Stahl, followed by VA Tech and Boehler.
The day's best performer was VA Stahl, up 3.49 percent at 489.50, while microchip producer AMS led decliners, losing 2.1 percent at 978.

Vienna airport operator Flughafen Wien recouped earlier losses to stand 6.55 schillings higher at 525.05 after saying it would raise its dividend to 16 schillings per share from 12 in 1995 despite posting an 11 percent fall in group net profit last year.
Flughafen attributed the decline in profits to a set of measures it had to take to "secure its long-term earnings potential."
The all-share Vienna bourse index added on 2.33 points, or 0.52 percent, at 447.5.
The April ATX future climbed 4.9 points to 1,174.1 on turnover of 1,043 contracts.
